title: What is C#
description: Understand C# and its role in .NET development.

data.text: **C#** (pronounced 'C Sharp') is a modern, object-oriented programming language developed by Microsoft in 2000 and led by chief architect Anders Hejlsberg. It was designed as part of the .NET initiative to provide a simple, type-safe, object-oriented language that compiles to intermediate language (IL) and runs on the Common Language Runtime (CLR).

C# was introduced alongside .NET Framework 1.0 in 2002. Its design was heavily influenced by Java, but with several improvements: properties, attributes, delegates, and unsafe code pointers. Since then, C# has evolved significantly with major language versions adding generics (C# 2.0), LINQ and lambda expressions (C# 3.0), async/await (C# 5.0), pattern matching (C# 7.0+), records and top-level statements (C# 9.0), and many more features in subsequent releases.

rows: Generics, nullable types, iterators, partial classes
LINQ, lambda expressions, extension methods, anonymous types
Pattern matching, tuples, local functions, ref returns
Primary constructors, collection expressions, inline arrays

data.text: C# remains one of the most popular programming languages worldwide. It combines the power of C++ with the ease of Visual Basic, offering a balanced approach that is both expressive and performant.

data.title: Key Advantages
items: **Modern language**: Continuously updated by Microsoft with annual releases and new features
**Type safety**: Static typing catches errors at compile time, reducing runtime crashes
**Versatile**: Used for web (ASP.NET), desktop (WinForms, WPF, MAUI), mobile (Xamarin/MAUI), games (Unity), cloud (Azure), and IoT
**Great tooling**: Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code with C# Dev Kit, and JetBrains Rider
**Large ecosystem**: .NET libraries, NuGet package registry with thousands of packages
**Cross-platform**: .NET Core/.NET 5+ runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS

data.text: C# is the primary language for the .NET platform. The .NET platform provides a runtime environment called the **Common Language Runtime (CLR)** that manages memory, handles exceptions, and provides security. It also includes the **Base Class Library (BCL)** with thousands of ready-to-use classes for common tasks.

When you compile C# code, the compiler produces **Intermediate Language (IL)** bytecode, which the CLR then **Just-In-Time (JIT)** compiles to native machine code when the application runs. This two-step compilation provides platform independence and security benefits.

data.text: The .NET ecosystem has grown dramatically. Today, .NET is a unified platform supporting multiple application types through a shared base library.

data.title: .NET Application Types
items: **ASP.NET Core** — Web applications, APIs, and microservices
**MAUI / Xamarin** — Cross-platform mobile and desktop apps
**Blazor** — Full-stack web apps with C# running in the browser via WebAssembly
**Azure Functions / AWS Lambda** — Serverless cloud functions
**.NET MAUI** — Cross-platform UI for mobile, desktop, and tablet

data.title: Open Source
data.text: Both C# and .NET are fully open source. The .NET runtime, compiler, and libraries are developed on GitHub (microsoft/dotnet) under the MIT license, with contributions welcomed from the community.

cards.title: Enterprise Web Apps
cards.description: ASP.NET Core powers high-performance web APIs and full-stack applications used by major companies.
cons: Steeper learning curve than Node.js for beginners

cards.title: Game Development
cards.description: Unity uses C# as its primary scripting language, making C# the most popular language for game development beyond C++.

cards.title: Cloud & Microservices

data.title: C# vs Other Languages
data.text: C# is often compared to Java — both are object-oriented and run on virtual machines. However, C# generally offers more language features ( LINQ, async/await, records, pattern matching ) and has evolved faster. It also compiles to native code on more platforms through .NET 5+.

items.question: Is C# free to use?
items.answer: Yes. C# and .NET are open source and free to use for any purpose, including commercial applications. Visual Studio Community Edition is also free for individual developers and small teams.

items.question: Can I run C# on Linux and macOS?
items.answer: Absolutely. Since .NET Core (now simply .NET), the platform is fully cross-platform. You can develop and deploy C# applications on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

items.question: Do I need Visual Studio to write C#?
items.answer: No. You can use Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit extension on any platform, or JetBrains Rider. Visual Studio provides the most features but is Windows-only in its full version.

items.question: What's the difference between C#, .NET, and Visual Studio?
items.answer: C# is the programming language. .NET is the platform/framework (runtime + libraries). Visual Studio is the IDE (Integrated Development Environment) that helps you write, debug, and build C# code.

items.question: Is C# only for Windows development?
items.answer: No. While C# was originally Windows-focused, .NET 5+ is fully cross-platform. You can build web apps, mobile apps (via MAUI), and desktop apps that run on any OS.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: C# is a modern, object-oriented language created by Microsoft in 2000
It compiles to IL which runs on the CLR via JIT compilation
C# is used for web, desktop, mobile, games, and cloud applications
It has evolved significantly from C# 1.0 to C# 12+
data.takeaway: C# is a versatile, mature language that continues to grow with modern development needs.
